summary: DAY adversarial review independently challenged all 12 active-batch companies against concentration, financing/dilution, accounting normalization, governance, substitution, execution and narrative-overreach failure modes. No current evidence forces a lane-specific promotion block for any of the 12; every name has material risks that can be handled reproducibly through conservative factor/risk treatment. Plausible future failure modes remain explicit and do not become blockers unless current sourced inputs are missing or contradictory.

companies.redTeamCase: The strongest bull evidence—large Meta/NVIDIA-linked demand and rapid capacity build—also creates the core failure path: concentrated counterparties, extraordinary capex, financing dependence and utilization risk. Treat contract value separately from margin/ROIC; do not assume five-gigawatt ambitions are economically accretive.
falsifiers: material delay/cancellation of committed customer capacity
rising capex without proportional contracted gross profit
liquidity stress or financing on increasingly punitive terms

companies.redTeamCase: Revenue/RPO can overstate durability if constellation replacement capex, government budget timing and customer concentration absorb economics. Cash/investments reduce near-term survival risk, but recurring satellite refresh and equity/convertible financing remain central to per-share value.
falsifiers: RPO conversion weakens materially
replacement capex rises faster than gross-profit growth
new financing materially expands dilution without demand payoff

companies.redTeamCase: The principal narrative trap is treating LOIs/master agreements as bankable contracted generation. Oklo remains pre-commercial and dependent on licensing, fuel, project finance and counterparty conversion. Large liquidity funded by equity/ATM extends runway but does not validate unit economics.
falsifiers: licensing milestones slip materially
framework counterparties do not convert to binding project contracts
project economics require structurally more dilution/capital than expected

companies.redTeamCase: Adjusted EBITDA can obscure negative GAAP gross profit/net loss and a capital-hungry mining build. AI-cloud optionality is real but still too small to justify underwriting the company as a mature AI-infrastructure operator. Crypto-cycle and financing risk must stay dominant until business mix changes.
falsifiers: continued GAAP gross losses despite hash-rate expansion
AI revenue fails to scale relative to self-mining capital needs
ATM/convertible issuance outpaces per-share cash-generation improvement

companies.redTeamCase: Fast revenue growth and manufacturing milestones can coexist with very high losses and acquisition complexity. SkyWater and other acquisitions create integration, dilution and capital-allocation risk; issuer roadmap claims must not be treated as proof of fault-tolerant commercial economics.
falsifiers: post-acquisition burn remains elevated without margin improvement
Superion deliveries slip or fail to convert to durable commercial revenue
acquisition integration creates recurring impairment/restructuring or further large equity issuance

companies.redTeamCase: Single-customer dependence is extreme enough that backlog and growth can create false comfort. Walmart-linked economics, deployment pacing, receivables and bargaining power should dominate concentration penalties until diversification is visible.
falsifiers: principal-customer deployment pauses or renegotiates economics
customer concentration remains near current levels while margins deteriorate
new customers fail to reach material revenue scale

companies.redTeamCase: AI/custom-silicon optimism can mask direct-customer, distributor and receivable concentration plus cyclical semiconductor/export exposure. Design-win headlines should be discounted unless accompanied by diversified revenue and cash conversion.
falsifiers: major direct/distributor customer loss
custom AI design concentration rises while gross margin/cash conversion weakens
export restrictions materially impair accessible demand

companies.redTeamCase: AI-optics growth is exposed to hyperscaler concentration, cycle duration and leverage. Pricing/yield gains may be cyclical rather than durable moat evidence; debt reduces tolerance for an optical downturn.
falsifiers: AI datacenter demand growth decelerates sharply
top-customer concentration rises alongside inventory/receivable stress
deleveraging stalls during margin compression

companies.redTeamCase: A one-time debt-extinguishment loss should be normalized, but the associated equity issuance is economically real. Concentrated hyperscaler demand and fast optical transitions create both upside and obsolescence risk.
falsifiers: share-count growth remains material after restructuring
1.6T/CPO transitions disintermediate current product economics
major-customer concentration rises as margins normalize downward

companies.redTeamCase: Strong margins/cash flow can hide channel and geography concentration. Distributor receivables and China/Taiwan exposure require conservative resilience treatment; outsourced manufacturing/capacity partners remain dependencies rather than owned moat.
falsifiers: channel inventory correction causes disproportionate revenue decline
Taiwan/China disruption materially limits supply or end demand
300mm expansion fails qualification or creates cost drag

companies.redTeamCase: Very rapid AI infrastructure growth and high customer concentration create classic peak-cycle risk. Revenue acceleration must be separated from margin durability, working-capital intensity and hyperscaler bargaining power.
falsifiers: top-customer growth reverses
working-capital/capex needs consume cash despite revenue growth
operating margin retraces as mix normalizes

companies.redTeamCase: Diversification is a genuine strength, but the 2026 acquisition wave creates the main failure path: integration complexity, debt, synergy optimism and capital-allocation risk. Acquired growth should not be mistaken for organic moat expansion without evidence.
falsifiers: integration costs/synergies miss guidance materially
leverage remains elevated while organic growth slows
large acquisitions reduce return on invested capital

contradictions: NBIS and SYM demonstrate that validated demand can increase concentration risk rather than reduce it.
IONQ's manufacturing progress is real evidence, but it does not validate roadmap economics or offset acquisition-related dilution/burn by itself.
BTDR's positive adjusted EBITDA does not negate current GAAP gross/net losses or capital intensity.
APH diversification lowers customer risk while acquisition concentration raises balance-sheet/integration risk.
unknowns: Exact live market crowding/short positioning is not a T0 underwriting input and is not fabricated.
Future regulatory, technology-transition and customer-renewal outcomes remain falsifiers, not current blockers unless sourced contradictions emerge.
peerRequests: Chief: all 12 names are red-team ready_for_chief, but apply explicit concentration/capital-structure penalties rather than reading readiness as endorsement.
Underwriting: retain conservative treatment for OKLO framework agreements and IONQ post-acquisition normalization.
Expectations-execution: flag NBIS/IONQ/OKLO narrative sensitivity and CLS/COHR/LITE/MRVL AI-cycle exposure without contaminating Earth Score.
